content:
The HAF programme
is a Department for Education initiative providing enriching
holiday activities and healthy meals for children eligible for free
school meals (FSM). HAF aims to reduce the “holiday
experience gap,” improving nutrition, and supporting
children’s wellbeing, as research shows that children from
low income families are more likely to have unhealthy food options
and experience social isolation during holidays.
DfE have awarded £1,655,070 per annum,
2026-2029, to Gloucestershire County Council to fund these
services. GCC have opted to distribute this via an open procurement
process to enable local delivery.
Following a
competitive tendering exercise, the Council was appointed as
district lead for Cheltenham Borough on 20 March. The role of the
District Lead Organisation is to develop, contract and deliver the
HAF programme in that District, to ensure that the provision meets
DFE requirements, and the DfE’s HAF contract standards.
In terms of the contract, legal advice has been sought and One
Legal are now satisfied that the contract poses no risks to the
Council.
Payments
The
administration payments to the council as district lead are as
follows:





District



Funding 
Spring 2026



Funding Summer 2026



Funding Winter 2026



Total





Cheltenham



£7,972



£31,887



£7,972



£47,831




 
Out of this
allocation, £30,300 will be taken as a contribution to CBC
overheads of administering the programme.
The delivery
allocations to the council for the purpose of subcontracting
activity providers for HAF programme delivery are as follows:





District



Funding 
Spring 2026



Funding Summer 2026



Funding Winter 2026



Total





Cheltenham



£26, 053



£104, 214

The Council undertakes due diligence checks on the providers to
ensure that the appropriate policies and procedures are in
place.
The Council
enters into grant agreements with the providers. The agreements set
out the conditions of funding, plus the DFE HAF Framework Standards
and arrangements for quality assessment checks.
 
Spring HAF 2026
Although the
council was not yet formally appointed as district lead, with GCC
agreement, we undertook an open and transparent process whereby
potential HAF providers were invited to submit bids via an online
platform. These were assessed by a panel comprising of the cabinet
lead, representative of GRCC (VCS infrastructure provider) and NCLB
officers. The programme was delivered from 1 April.
The Spring HAF programme comprised 13 delivery partners, at a cost
of £25,990 to deliver just under 850 spaces over a 4-day
period. Details of the Spring delivery plan are supplied in
Appendix A.

Summer HAF 2026
The bidding
process for summer HAF delivery opened on 29 April 2026 and again
providers were invited to submit bids via an online platform
– with closing date of 27 May
Potential
providers were also invited to attend an in-person prospective HAF
provider event on 5 May. This session was held to outline local
processes and priorities for HAF delivery in Cheltenham and provide
an opportunity for prospective providers to discuss potential
delivery areas. After presenting processes and priorities, CBC
staff left the event leaving a rep from the Children’s
Society to facilitate an informal discussion with providers to
explore opportunities to collaborate on bids.
In total, 23 bids
were received, requesting a total of £172k. These were
assessed by a panel comprising of the cabinet lead, representative
of GRCC (VCS infrastructure provider) and NCLB officers.
The delivery plan is attached as
Appendix B that includes 19 providers – including
CBC-facilitated Party in the Park with an allocation of
£10k.
 
 
Background information:
 
Core
Requirements for the District Lead
Organisation.

•             
The provider must have a base of operations in the
district they are delivering in.

•             
Have the responsibility in their district to ensure
that the programme meets DFE requirements for the HAF Programme
detailed below.

•             
Be ambassadors and champions of the Gloucestershire
HAF programme, working in partnership with other District Leads,
GCC HAF team and other key stakeholders to maximise the impact of
the programme and its resources in Gloucestershire.

•             
To develop a focus group to include the voice of the
young person in planning for the HAF programme.

•             
Work with GCC HAF team to agree providers for each
HAF holiday to reach FSM children and young people in the
district.

•             
Ensure all schools in the district are aware of and
engaged in the HAF programme, with adequate representation on the
Stakeholder network.

•             
Work with activity providers and provide
opportunities to ensure children, young people, and families in
their district are actively shaping provision.

•             
To arrange and chair district provider meetings
ensuring all district providers are aware of any updates and have
the space to air any challenges or concerns.

•             
To work with the Council to agree monitoring
questions for activity providers

•             
To bear the responsibility of your district
providers updating and uploading registers and monitoring forms and
contacting those providers who have not uploaded or updating
registers on the Family Hubs booking system.

•             
Provide monitoring and evaluation information in
line with agreed deadlines.

•             
To ensure subcontracted providers are providing the
required due diligence to the Council.

•             
To work towards the goals and targets as set out in
the Council’s One Plan

content:
To approve the award of a
contract to Bay Media
Ltd for the manufacture,
installation, maintenance and removal of advertising banners on
lamp posts across Cheltenham, and to authorise the Council to enter
into the contract.

The Council undertook a
competitive procurement exercise via the In-tend procurement portal
for the provision of lamp post advertising banner services. The
procurement was undertaken following the previous supplier ceasing
to trade and the implementation of temporary arrangements to ensure
continuity of service. The competitive procurement exercise secures
a compliant, long-term contractual arrangement for the Council.
Four compliant tenders were received and evaluated against the
published quality and price criteria. Bay Media Ltd achieved the
highest overall evaluation score of 90,
demonstrating the most economically advantageous tender and
offering the best overall value for money. Approval is therefore
sought to award the contract to Bay Media Ltd and enter into the
contract.

The Council considered
continuing the interim contractual arrangements that were put in
place following the previous supplier ceasing to trade. However, as
these arrangements were temporary, this option was rejected in
favour of undertaking a competitive procurement exercise to secure
a long-term contract that delivers best value and complies with the
Council's procurement requirements.

The procurement specification
and evaluation methodology were developed by the relevant Council
officers. The opportunity was advertised through the In-tend
procurement portal and tender submissions were evaluated by an
officer evaluation panel in accordance with the published
evaluation criteria.
topline: The Cabinet Member Economic Development, Wellbeing, Culture and Public Open Space has decided to award a contract to Bay Media Ltd for advertising banners on lamp posts in Cheltenham.

content:
The Wilson is a
museum accredited by Arts Council England. The museum collections
are under the custodianship of the Council and are managed by the
Cheltenham Trust under the management agreement between the Council
and the Trust for the delivery of leisure and culture
services.

In order to maintain, develop and safeguard the collections for
future generations, the Council and the Trust will keep the
collections under review in line with the Interim Collections
Development Policy.

The items identified in the attached Appendix 1 are from the
Council’s taxidermy collection, and date back to the
Edwardian era. These items are deteriorating, and because arsenic
and mercury were historically used in the preservation process,
harmful chemicals are now being released into the air within the
storage area—the Museum’s tower.

This poses risks for CBC staff and external contractors who must
access the area, requiring them to wear full PPE, which increases
maintenance costs for CBC.

To address the issue, the Curatorial team at The Wilson have
completed their due diligence on the items and these will be
disposed of because they are classed as a health and safety hazard
due to the presence of toxic chemicals such as arsenic, mercury and
copper.

By disposing of these objects from the Council’s collections
the Council is ensuring that the health and safety risks, legal and
regulatory risks, financial risks, operational risks and
reputational risks of not disposing of the objects has been
mitigated.

This disposal due to health and safety risks enables the Council to
ensure it can maintain, develop and safeguard the museum
collections for the future generations of the people of
Cheltenham.

The items identified in the attached Appendix 2 will be disposed of
via direct gift to another accredited museum as they relate more
closely to the Collections Development Policies of the Dean
Heritage Centre, Milestones Museum and Eyam Museum.

By disposing of these objects from the Council’s collections
via direct gift to another accredited museum it is possible for
these objects to be shared with and enjoyed by communities and
audiences within a more appropriate context.

This transfer via direct gift enables the Council to ensure it can
maintain, develop and safeguard the museum collections for the
future generations of the people of Cheltenham.
Background information:   Interim Collections Development Policy
2025-2027
topline: The Head of Communities, Wellbeing and Partnerships has decided to dispose of deteriorating taxidermy items from the Council's collection due to health and safety risks.

content:
To appoint, (in consultation with the Chair
and Vice Chair of Overview and Scrutiny) a Scrutiny Task Group in
accordance with Rule 2.8 Part 4D of the Council’s
Constitution, to perform the function of a Joint Scrutiny Panel for
the purpose of scrutinising the Local Government Reorganisation
Portfolio within Gloucestershire. 

1.1   
The seven existing Gloucestershire councils (Gloucestershire County
Council, Gloucester City Council, Cheltenham Borough Council,
Tewkesbury Borough Council, Stroud District Council, Cotswolds
District Council and Forest of Dean District Council) (“the
Participating Councils”) are currently progressing work
associated with Local Government Reorganisation (LGR).

 
1.2   
 The Participating Councils have agreed
to set up a Joint Scrutiny Panel (“the Joint Scrutiny
Panel”) in order to provide accountability for the LGR
Portfolio and those charged with delivering it.
 
1.3   
 The Joint Scrutiny Panel is established
to provide cross-council, non-executive and non decision-making scrutiny of the process for LGR
across Gloucestershire, including the arrangements for governance,
decision-making, finance, engagement, evidence and
transparency.
 
1.4   
 The Joint Scrutiny Panel is set up by
Cheltenham Borough Council as a Scrutiny Task Group (STG) in
accordance with Part 4D para 2.8 of Cheltenham Borough
Council’s Constitution. Two Members from each of the
Participating Councils will be co-opted onto the STG in accordance
with the Terms of Reference for the STG which will be agreed
formally at the first meeting of the STG.

The Participating Councils could each
scrutinise the LGR process individually or a formal joint scrutiny
committee or sub-committee could be established.  
 
These options were considered by the Leaders
of the Participating Councils and the option of a Joint Scrutiny
Panel hosted by Cheltenham Borough Council was chosen as the
preferred option.

None declared.

All the Participating Councils’ Overview
and Scrutiny Committees were consulted on the proposal to set up a
joint scrutiny arrangement and the various options available. There
was overall support for the preferred option put forward to set up
a Joint Scrutiny Panel. The Chair and Vice Chair of Overview and
Scrutiny have been consulted in relation to the decision to appoint
the STG as required by Part 4D para 2.8 of the
Constitution.
topline: The Director of Governance, Housing and Communities and Monitoring Officer has decided to appoint a Scrutiny Task Group to scrutinise the Local Government Reorganisation Portfolio within Gloucestershire.

content:
To sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) that sets out the joint
council governance regarding the Local Government Reorganisation
(LGR) Reserve held by Gloucestershire County Council to fund the
necessary transformation to move to unitarisation of local
government in Gloucestershire.


The total cost of delivering Local Government
Reorganisation (LGR) in Gloucestershire has been currently
estimated to range from circa £21m to £30m to deliver
LGR in Gloucestershire, assuming that either one or two unitary
authorities are created.

It has been agreed that a joint reserve is created,
funded by contributions from all Gloucestershire councils, and held
by Gloucestershire County Council.

Subject to agreement by every council, the split in
the composition of funding has been agreed in principle as
follows:


55% to be contributed GCC

45% to be contributed by the District Councils in
equal shares.


As the holder of the LGR reserves, formally, this
will mean legal accountability sits with GCC. Therefore a
Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) has been drafted to ensure that a
partnership approach is taken, and there is collective ownership
and oversight of decision-making. Alongside this, arrangements are
for a joint scrutiny of the Programmeis
being established.

The MoU will clarify the principles and controls by
which the pooled budget will operate. It sets out what expenditure
will be eligible to be funded from this budget, which is likely to
be limited to those activities which are:


Related to LGR and additional to current council
services and responsibilities.

In support of defined and agreed plans within the
LGR portfolio.

Related to budgeted expenditure items such as
staffing capacity, technical advice, programme delivery,
redundancies, ICT systems, the aggregation and disaggregation of
services, and communications.

 


Councils could hold on to funding individually but,
due to the expected pace at which transformation and change is
needed to meet the expected mobilisation of new councils it is
considered a significant administrative demand if LGR mobilisation
was funded in a decentralised way.
 


The MOU has been drafted in consultation with all seven local
authorities
topline: The Chief Executive has decided to sign a Memorandum of Understanding to govern the Local Government Reorganisation Reserve in Gloucestershire.

content:
The Data,
Analysis and Insights Team at Gloucestershire County Council
provides research and information services to a range of
Gloucestershire partner authorities. These services are known as
MAIDeN services, the acronym standing for Multi-Agency Information
Database for Neighbourhoods.

The ‘MAIDeN services enable Gloucestershire districts and
partners (including voluntary organisations and Parish and Town
Councils) to access products and services provided by the Data and
Analysis Team - Gloucestershire County Council via
https://www.gloucestershire.gov.uk/inform/

The ‘MAIDeN services also includes access to a dedicated
resource to help you with bespoke data, information or intelligence
requests.

The full list of services that are available are as follows:







 



Description





Community safety reports



Monthly interactive reports showing numbers and
rates (using maps, graphs and tables) for a range of crimes
including; criminal damage, ASB, domestic burglary, racist
incidents, class A drug offences, young victims of
crime.

This gives access to some data that is not publicly
available at this level of geography.





Accessibility toolkit



This toolkit is updated bi-annually and provides our calculations of the drive and
public transport journey times to key predefined services in the
county.





Unemployment bulletin



A monthly bulletin providing an analysis of the
latest unemployment data at county, district and ward
level.





Population analysis of the protected
characteristics



This interactive report provides an overview of the
population of Gloucestershire by the nine protected
characteristics, where possible information goes down to ward
level.





Overview reports



A series of reports summarising the key issues for a
particular topic. Current topics include Economy, Population,
Community Safety, Accessibility, Adults and Older People, Children
and Young People, Deprivation and Environment.





Additional products



Additional products published on Inform
Gloucestershire, using newly released data e.g. Census
reports





Housing and Employment Land Database



Hosting and managing the Housing and Employment Land
Database.





Parish Profiles



We commission the production of a profile for each
parish in the county. The profiles cover topics including
Population, Vulnerable Groups, Housing, Education and Skills,
Economy, Access and Transport, Crime and Safety, Communities and
Environment and Health and Wellbeing





Use of OCSI



Use of the OCSI tool Local Insight. Local Insight
can support you with strategic planning and service delivery by
providing up-to-date information and analysis of your local
communities. Based on up-to-date open data, Local Insight enables
you to map over 100 social and economic indicators against your
communities.





Access to customer segmentation data



Customer segmentation data groups the UK population
by shared characteristics. By analysing demographic data, social
factors, population and consumer behaviour, it provides precise
information and an understanding of different types of people.
Acorn provides valuable consumer insight helping you target,
acquire and develop profitable customer relationships and improve
service delivery.





Newsletter



A regular newsletter detailing new products
available.





Named Contact



A named person to contact when the partner has
questions or needs information.





Ad Hoc Enquires (less than 4 hours per
enquiry)



Ability to contact the team with a reasonable number
of small enquiries (less than 4 hours) on an ad hoc
basis. 





Ad Hoc Enquires  (that
take between 4 hours and 4 days)



Ability to contact the team with small enquiries
(that take up to 1-4 days) on an ad hoc basis.





Bespoke accessibility enquiries to support
SHLA



In order to support the SHLA we regularly carry out
bespoke enquires for most districts that involve calculating travel
time from potential development sites to local
facilities.






Recent support from the GCC Research team include support to
analyse the recently published Indices of Deprivation and compiling
data to support the Council’s bid to retain Purple Flag
status for the night-time economy.

In addition, the council has access to the Local Insight which
enables the council to collate and map data across 100 social and
economic indicators for a range of geographies including
wards.

content:
To award a contract to Tallis Amos Ltd to supply one
Trimax Pegasus S5 Triple Deck Gang Mower at a total cost of
£40,175.00 plus VAT


Ubico, on behalf of Cheltenham Borough Council,
deliver environmental services, including grounds maintenance,
across the Borough.

A tractor?trailed cylinder gang mower that is on the
fleet to support grass?cutting is now five years old, no longer
reliable and beyond economical repair. 
This specific type of cylinder mower is no longer
manufactured.  A rotary gang mower is
now the most suitable replacement option and they are mechanically
simpler with fewer moving and wearing parts making them easier and
more cost?effective to maintain compared with the old
cylinder?based systems. This change in technology will improve
reliability and reduce whole?life costs for the service.

A procurement exercise has been carried out via the
TPPL framework.


Officers have considered whether the service could continue to be
delivered without this equipment and concluded that it could not
given the authority’s commitment to maintain its green open
spaces and grass verges.  The existing
equipment is old and beyond economical repair.


Internal consultation has taken place with relevant
officers.  The Cabinet Member has been
consulted.  Officers and the cabinet
member agree there is a need to procure this equipment to continue
to deliver services and minimise revenue costs.

content:
To award a contract to Cardo (Wales and West)
Limited for the purposes of replacing the existing combustible high
risk external cladding system to 3no 5 storey blocks of flats

Essential remedial fire safety works
identified in the Fire Risk Assessments need to be carried out to
3no 5 storey blocks of flats (Arle
Road, Orchard Way and Grevil Road). The
scope of work includes:
 

·        
Replacement of External wall insulation (EWI) to the external walls
with new finishes provided.

·        
Decentralized Mechanical Extract Ventilation (dMEV) provided to all apartment wet rooms.

·        
Isolated loft insulation works to ensure loft insulation overlaps
the new EWI insulation at the building eaves.

·        
Structural repair works.
 
Following a call off from the South West
Procurement Alliance (SWPA) Framework Agreement for Fire Safety
Cladding Remediation, Cardo (Wales and West) Limited have been
successful.
 
The procurement exercise confirmed that they
meet all the required criteria for experience and technical
knowledge of the property type and its construction.
An intent to award (subject to Cabinet
approval) letter has been sent to Cardo (Wales and West) Limited
and the price is held until 30th June 2026.

The Council considered utilising an existing
contract with retrofit External Wall Insulation (EWI) contractors
delivering social housing decarbonisation works across existing
housing stock. However, the size and complexity of this project was
compared against the existing resources, skills and proven
capabilities and it requires a significantly increased proven level
of specialist expertise and experience. 
 
It was determined that a specific contract
would be lower risk and provide the better value for money for the
Council.   Due to the combustible
cladding being identified on successive fire risk assessments as
high-risk, this is essential fire safety works that must be
delivered as planned to ensure the risk to residents is
removed.

Consultation has taken place with
Gloucestershire fire and rescue service, structural engineers,
building control, ward members, planning officers and block
residents. The feedback received has been very positive from all
parties especially by block residents concerned about the long-term
viability of their homes.
topline: The Cabinet Member Housing and Customer Services has decided to award a contract to replace combustible cladding on 3 blocks of flats for essential fire safety works.

content:
To enter into a Pre-Construction Service Agreement (PCSA) with the
Preferred Contractor to deliver pre-construction services and
activities for the Project at the former Monkscroft School Site.

Following completion of the PCSA services, and subject to the costs
of delivery being within the approved budget envelope, approve the
construction of 70 units of affordable housing, and associated
development, by the Preferred Contractor at the former Monkscroft School Site in accordance with the
planning permission.

To delegate authority to the Director of Construction, Properties
and Assets in consultation with Cabinet Member for Housing, the
Section 151 Officer and Director One Legal to agree the terms of
and enter into the PCSA, the main construction contract with the
Preferred Contractor and all other legal agreements or other
documentation as may be required to implement or facilitate the
development.



On 3rd March 2020, Cabinet resolved to purchase the
former Monkscroft School Site for the development of affordable
housing to be owned by the Authority. It was noted that the Cabinet
Member for housing has delegated authority to approve the number of
dwellings to be provided and will authorise the award of contracts
for the construction of the housing above
£100,000.  The Council has
purchased the site and planning permission has recently been
obtained and to enable the Council to deliver The Monkscroft School
project it is first necessary to enter into a Pre-Construction
Services Agreement with a third party to complete the required
design development, surveys and other services. This will determine
a fixed cost price for the development with reduced risks ahead of
executing a JCT Design & Build Contract with a Principal
Contractor.

A procurement exercise has taken place and following receipt of
three compliant bids the preferred contactor was selected. This
decision notice provides the relevant authority to enter the
necessary contracts with the Preferred Contractor.

Once the services under the PCSA have been completed, the Council
will have received fully designed and costed proposals and will
then decide whether it will proceed with the construction of the
development, Subject to budget approval, the Director of
Construction, Properties and Assets in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Housing, the Section 151 Officer
and Director One Legal is granted delegated authority to
proceed with the development and enter into the JCT D&B
contract with the Preferred Contractor referred to in the attached
tender acceptance report.


CBC officers determined that contracting with a third party would
be lower risk and would provide the best value for money for the
Council.  


The site and associated development proposals have been discussed
at the overarching governance structure overseeing the CBC’s
affordable homes programme, which includes the Strategic Housing
Delivery Group (SHDG) and Cabinet Member Housing Working Group
(CMHWG).

Procurement strategies have been discussed with the Affordable
Housing Project Board, which is being reported to 3 times a year;
Cabinet Lead and several members of the Leadership Team sit on that
Board.

Further, Cabinet Lead for Major Development and Housing Delivery is
briefed once a month, Senior Leadership Team 3 times a year, and
full briefing to Leader of the Cabinet every month.

CBC identify the redevelopment of the Monkscroft school site as one of the key priorities
for the council, and the appointment of the Design and Build
Construction contractor is central to realising this aim.

The procurement exercise has been completed working closely with
Publica Procurement and assistance from
One Legal and legal firm Ashfords
LLP

Regular reporting will continue via the current governance
arrangements for new supply including the affordable housing
project board, Cabinet/Council as required and discussions between
CBC officers and senior management.
topline: The Cabinet Member Major Developments and Housing Delivery has decided to proceed with the construction of affordable housing at the former Monkscroft School Site.

This decision updates the Cotswold Beechwoods Special Areas of Conservation (SAC)
mitigation fees by 14.68% in line with Retail Price Index (RPI)
(ONS), ensuring the contribution levels remain consistent with
those applied across all participating authorities. All local
planning authorities (LPAs) affected by the Strategy have agreed to
apply the same RPI?based uplift to maintain consistency in
mitigation funding. The new rates will apply from 1st
April 2026.
 


There is a legal requirement to mitigate impacts on the
Beechwoods SAC. The Cotswolds
Beechwoods Mitigation Strategy was
adopted first by Stroud in October 2022 and then subsequently by
the other relevant councils. Cheltenham Cabinet adopted the
Strategy 2nd April
2024.

The Strategy details the original costs for the Strategic Access
Management Monitoring (SAMM); Strategic Alternative Natural
Greenspace (SANGS), these are consistent across all the affected
LPAs. The LPAs also charge an administrative/legal fee, and in some
instances, there is also a monitoring fee.

The fees need to be increased in line with inflation reflecting
with the provision set out in the Strategy. Indexation has been
applied from October 2022, the point at which the Strategy was
first adopted by Stroud District Council. An RPI increase of 14.68%
has been applied, calculated from RPI All
Items Index: Jan 1987=100 - Office for National Statistics.
This shows that in October 2022 the RPI index was 356.2 whereas it
had increased by 52.3 points (14.68%) to 408.5 by December
2025.
 

Section 106 Fee Structure

Two S106 routes exist, each requiring different levels of
administration and monitoring.

i)            
Where the Mitigation Contribution is paid on completion of the S106, the administration/legal fee is
lower due to minimal ongoing officer involvement.

ii)           
Where payment is on commencement of
development, additional legal checks and future monitoring are
required, giving rise to a higher administration/legal fee plus a
monitoring fee.

Mitigation Contribution is on Completion of the S106

content:
To enter into a contract with Dean Martin
Contractors Ltd for the purposes of:
 

•     
Desilting Hatherley Lake,

•     
Transporting the silt to an amenity grassland area for reuse,
and

•     
Constructing planted revetments
 
The contract value is £39,535 and is
subject to receiving planning approval by 
Planning Committee on 19th February 2026.
 
The works are required to:
 

•     
Restore water depth and storage capacity

•     
Improve water quality

•     
Support fish and aquatic habitats

•     
Reduce flood risk

•     
Prevent odour, stagnation and decline in amenity value

•     
Ensure the long-term sustainability of the lake.

To enable the Council to desilt Hatherley lake, improve water quality and the
biodiversity of the lake it is necessary to enter into a contract
with a third party to deliver the works and provide project
management services.
A request-for-quotation exercise was issued
through the eprocurement portal for
contracts between £30,000 and £60,000. 4 quotations
were received, several exceeded the procurement bracket. Following
assessment of quotations received, Dean Martin Contractors Ltd
provided best value.
 
Publica
Procurement advised that normally a further competitive tender
would be best practice. However, the project is time?sensitive, and delays from re?tendering would negatively impact ecology, lake recovery
and environmental conditions:
 

•     
Winter is the optimal period for desilting to minimise disruption
to wildlife and park users.

•     
If works continue into early spring, mitigation measures will be
implemented.

•     
An independent ecologist is in place to provide guidance.
 
In this case the works are urgently required
and cannot be delayed further by readvertising.
 
Given the urgency and the transparency of the
quotation process, a waiver is required.
 
Background
information
£50,000 capital (CAP113) has been
secured for this project and £5,000 through a contribution
from the Friends of Hatherley.
 
An Ecological Impact assessment and Flood Risk
assessment have been completed and are publicly available as part
of a planning application 25/01931/FUL. The contract is subject to
decision making at 
Planning Committee on the 19th February 2026.

To undertake a competitive procurement
exercise. This has been discounted due to the urgent need for works
and the narrow seasonal window.
 
I have actioned officers to work with the
procurement team on a lesson learned review outside of this
process.

As Director of Planning & Building
Control, both the planning team and
green spaces team fall within my portfolio. I
confirm that:
 

•     
I have had no involvement in the planning application, which has
been managed independently by the case officer and Head of
Planning.

•     
I have not participated in the procurement process, which has been
managed

•     
independently by the Community Parks Development Officer and Parks
and Public Realm Manager.

The Friends of Hatherley Park have been consulted on this project
and have supported with
additional funding.
 
The lead officer has had ongoing engagement
with:
 

•     
Publica Procurement,

•     
Finance Business Partner

•     
OneLegal

•     
Trees officer

•     
Drainage and Flood Risk Engineer
 
The Cabinet member for Waste, Recycling,
Parks, Gardens and Green Open Space is supportive of the project
and has been kept informed.
topline: The Director of Planning & Building Control has decided to enter into a contract with Dean Martin Contractors Ltd to desilt Hatherley Lake and improve water quality.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member Housing and Customer Services
content:
To enter into contract with the successful
supplier (jointly, along with our commissioning partners, details
of which are set out below) to provide a range of additional
security measures for maintaining victim safety at home, otherwise
known as Target Hardening and Sanctuary Scheme measures. This
contract will be for a period of three years from 01 April 2026 to
31 March 2029, with options to extend the contract annually
thereafter, up to 31 March 2033, subject to relevant approvals and
available finance.

The aim of this
Target Hardening and Sanctuary service is to prevent homelessness
and to keep victims and their children safe in their own homes,
protecting them from further harm whilst also promoting safety and
well-being for victims of domestic abuse and their children.

This will be achieved through the provision of a range of
additional security measures, ranging from the installation of
security devices which can be fitted readily to buildings without
major adaption, through to Sanctuary provision. The latter is a
more extensive fitment of security measures which can include a
‘sanctuary room’ to provide a safe place where victims
can call and await the arrival of the police.

Gloucester City Council has led on the commissioning of this
service via the county-wide Partnership Team. Cheltenham Borough
Council will enter into contract with the successful supplier
alongside: Cotswold District Council, Forest of Dean District
Council, Gloucester City Council, Stroud District Council,
Tewkesbury Borough Council, Gloucestershire Fire and Rescue Service
(as part of Gloucestershire County Council) and the Office of the
Police and Crime Commissioner (OPCC).

Aside from an annual contribution from the OPCC, the funding for
this contract operates as a ‘pay as you go’ service to
meet the demand for the scheme. Each district authority will be
responsible for ordering and paying for the services directly.
Having reviewed costs incurred so far for 2025/26 and for 2024/25,
we anticipate the council’s costs to be around
£25,000/year. These costs will be met from the
council’s Homelessness Prevention Grant Funding allocation.
This is funding which the council receives each year from the
Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government to support
the delivery of initiatives such as this.
topline: The Cabinet Member Housing and Customer Services has decided to enter into a contract to provide security measures for maintaining victim safety at home.

content:
At a 
meeting of Planning Committee on 29th May 2025, Cheltenham
Borough Council agreed to approve application 16/02000/OUT, subject
to the prior signing of a S106. A period of 9 months was provided
to complete the S106.  This is a
cross-boundary application and the Planning Committee of Tewkesbury
Borough Council also made the decision to approve the scheme
subject to the signing of S106, which was delegated to Tewkesbury
Borough Council’s Director of Growth.


The following was agreed by Cheltenham Planning Committee:

To delegate authority to the Head of Planning to permit the
application subject to:

A) the conditions as set out or substantially similar as may be
agreed under delegated authority given to the Head of Planning;
and

B) completion of a S106 obligation to deliver the infrastructure
and other mitigation, as set out in this report at paragraphs 8.506
and 8.510, and for alterations to s106 heads of terms as may be
agreed under delegated authority given to the Head of Planning in
consultation with the Chairman and Vice Chairman of the Planning
Committee.

C) In the event that the S106 agreement remains unsigned nine
months after this resolution, that the application is reviewed by
the Head of Planning in consultation with the Chairman and Vice
Chairman of the Planning Committee, and if no progress is being
made delegated authority is given to the Head of Planning to refuse
the application in the absence of an agreed S106 Agreement.

This officer decision relates to criterion (C) of that
decision.

Since the decision was made by the Planning Committee, the local
planning authority has remained in close engagement with the
applicant. This includes a monthly meeting between the Agent, the
Director of Planning & Building Control (Cheltenham) and the
Director of Growth (Tewkesbury).

There are 2 principal reasons why progress has not been made to the
extent that the timescale as agreed by Planning Committee can be
met:

1. This is a strategic scheme and post the decision further
extensive cost planning work was undertaken by the applicant, this
is key information that will support the applicant’s inputs
into the S106. Officers have been kept informed of this work.

2. The S106 will be a tripartite agreement between the local
planning authorities, the applicant and Gloucestershire County
Council. There have been key capacity challenges in legal support
via the County Council, officers have been engaging actively on
this point and the County Council confirmed on 14th January 2026
that an external legal firm has been appointed to support the
County Council in delivery. This capacity challenge has been
outside the control of either the local planning authority or the
applicant.

On this basis, it is appropriate to extend the period of time for
the signing of the S106, and through this officer decision this is
extended to 30th October 2026.

Given this is a cross-boundary planning application, an officer
decision is also being made by Tewkesbury Borough Council.

content:
To approve a shortened version of the template
partnership agreement with green space volunteer groups, which was
approved at Cabinet on 18 February 2025 as part of the updated
volunteering policy. 
 


The template partnership agreement was introduced in
February 2025 for use with the constituted green space volunteer
groups that volunteer regularly on council land under their own
insurance. 

The aim of the agreement is to set out clearly the
responsibilities on both sides to enable constituted groups to
volunteer more autonomously and flexibly through a clear, safe and
supportive process.  It will also reduce
the capacity demands on the Green Space Development team from the
growing number of groups operating and enable a fair distribution
of support and time to support potential new groups.  

Following feedback from the groups, the template
agreement has been shortened and simplified to make it more
workable for the groups, while still retaining the key
points.  The document has also been
renamed ‘partnership pledge’ rather than
‘partnership agreement’ following feedback and in
recognition that groups are volunteering from good will and that
the document is not intended to be a legally binding
contract.
 


The council could continue with the previously
approved template partnership agreement but the risk is that many
of the green space volunteer groups would not be willing to sign up
to it as it is too long and daunting. 

The council could also revert to not having an
agreement in place with the green space volunteer groups, but that
leaves the responsibilities on both sides less clearly demarcated,
which increases capacity demands on the green space development
team and leaves groups in confusion about what their commitments
are. 
 


The draft revised partnership pledge was discussed
with the green space volunteer groups in August 2025 and they also
submitted further written feedback on it in the following
weeks. 

The groups recognised the positives of the
partnership pledge in ensuring equality between groups and giving
them flexibility to volunteer outside council working hours, as
often as they like and to achieve more and benefit from funding
opportunities to improve the green spaces. 

However, some of the groups had concerns about
responsibilities including GDPR, holding personal data for their
volunteers, safeguarding and the level of administrative time
needed.  There was also clarity needed
about insurance requirements.

Gloucestershire Rural Community Council has been
involved in supporting the groups and a number of them are willing
to sign the partnership pledge.  Some of
the groups are not ready to do this and their volunteers will
remain as council volunteers, under council supervision and
insurance.  They will be reliant on the
capacity of the green space development team to run sessions, and
the number of sessions per group will be reviewed to ensure
fairness in line with capacity.
topline: The Cabinet Member Safety and Communities has decided to approve a shortened 'partnership pledge' agreement for green space volunteer groups.

To revoke a number of Supplementary
Planning Guidance and Supplementary Planning Documents so that they
will no longer be used for decision-making purposes.

 

 

 
 

RESOLVED THAT:
 

1.   
the list of SPGs, SPDs and the Urban Design
Concept Statements informal guidance notes set out in Table 1 at
paragraph 3.5 of this report are formally revoked and withdrawn
from publication
 


To revoke a number of Supplementary
Planning Guidance notes (SPGs) and Supplementary Planning Documents
(SPDs). Over approximately the past 30 years, Cheltenham Borough
Council has produced a number of SPGs and SPDs to help guide
development. Planning guidance such as SPGs and SPDs are capable of
being a material consideration in decision making.

 

Some of these documents have become
increasingly out of date and some of them are based on policies in
the Development Plan that no longer exist. Furthermore, various
national planning changes have taken place.

 

Cheltenham Borough Council is in the
process of updating its website and it is therefore considered an
opportune time to review the current suite of SPGs and SPDs and
revoke any that are no longer relevant. This will provide clarity
for all users of the planning system.
 


There is no statutory requirement to publicly

decision_maker: Cabinet Member Waste, Recycling, Parks, Gardens and Green Open Space
content:
To
award a contract to Tetra Tech Limited to deliver a costed options
appraisal/feasibility study and indicative layout/size for a new
future proofed fit for purpose combined depot site either on the
existing site in Swindon Road or an alternative location suitable
for a strategic waste site for the sum of
£34,390.

To allocate a £16,666 CIL
funding contribution from Cheltenham Borough Council into the
£150,000 CIL allocation which will fund the strategic waste
site feasibility project.  This contract award is the first
milestone in this project which is funded from the £150,000
CIL contribution plus CIL contributions from each of the partner
authorities, who are Cheltenham, Tewkesbury and Gloucestershire
County Council, with a total budget of £200,000 to fund the
strategic waste site feasibility project to formal
decision.


The existing depot site at Swindon Road Cheltenham which has been
operating since the 1950’s under old permits including
exemptions is now old, expensive to maintain and will be unable to
meet future service needs.  The site,
owned by Cheltenham, now services two waste collection authorities,
Cheltenham Borough Council and Tewkesbury Borough Council for
waste, recycling, street cleansing and grounds maintenance
services. Gloucestershire County Council as the disposal authority
has a strategic interest in future provision of household recycling
centre capacity and waste disposal options within the
County. 

All three authorities now require a costed options appraisal and
indicative layout/size for a new future proofed fit for purpose
combined depot site either on the existing site in Swindon Road or
an alternative location suitable for a strategic waste site which
meets future waste collection and disposal service needs.


Officers and members have considered whether the project could be
progressed without this feasibility study to identify costs, land
availability, permitting and planning constraints and concluded
that a formal decision will require detailed costings amongst other
information to take forward such significant
expenditure.  There is insufficient
inhouse expertise or capacity to deliver this work and therefore it
needs to be outsourced.


Internal consultation has taken place with relevant
officers within all three authorities. 
The Cabinet Member Waste and Recycling and Parks, Gardens and Green
Open Spaces has been consulted. 
Officers and the cabinet member agree there is a need to commission
the feasibility study in conjunction with partner authorities to
facilitate the provision of a new strategic waste site.
topline: The Cabinet Member Waste, Recycling, Parks, Gardens and Green Open Space has decided to award a contract for a feasibility study for a new waste site in Cheltenham.

decision_maker: Director of Governance, Housing and Communities and Monitoring Officer - Claire Hughes
content:
The purpose of
this Local Lettings Plan is to support Cottsway’s investment
into one hundred and forty (140) new-build affordable homes (of
which 98 social rented and affordable rented homes are covered by
this Local Lettings Plan) at Shurdington Road, Cheltenham, GL53
0JH, by setting out the appropriate measures required to strike a
reasonable balance between meeting the local authority’s
housing needs and supporting the establishment of a new,
sustainable and cohesive community in this location through
sensitive lettings arrangements.
For context, this
area has a comparatively low level of existing affordable housing
stock, and thus the introduction of a significant volume of
affordable homes (including 98 no. rented homes) must be carefully
managed to ensure that the existing and new community in this area
have the best opportunity to thrive.

This Local Lettings Plan will provide Cottsway with greater control
over first lets to minimise the risk of persons with significant
support needs being housed on this development covering the initial
first let period. Nevertheless, to meet the Council’s housing
needs, the Local Lettings Plan commits Cottsway to letting these
properties to households in priority housing need (Emergency, Gold
or Silver band) as identified on the Council’s housing
register.
From a Corporate perspective, creating quality
homes and safe and strong communities is a key priority of the

Council’s new Corporate Plan (2025-2028). Under this
priority, the Council has committed to- “Build positive
connections with our communities, make people feel safer and
improve our neighbourhoods and public spaces”. The Corporate
Plan also acknowledges that the Council and Cottsway (in our
capacity as providers of social housing) must meet the requirements
outlined within the new consumer standards set out by the Regulator
of Social Housing (RSH), especially, (in the context of this local
lettings plan) concerning the 
Neighbourhood and Community Standard, which requires that we
(and Cottsway(- “engage with partners including police, the
voluntary sector charities to ensure that tenants can live in safe
and well maintained neighbourhoods as well as feeling safe in their
homes”.

Both of these corporate and national drivers are consistent with
the introduction of a Local Lettings Plan on this large new-build
development.
The focus on creating strong, healthy communities is reinforced
further within the 
Council’s Housing, Homelessness and Rough Sleeping Strategy
2023 to 2028, with Priority 5 of the strategy being- “We
will invest in our communities to help make them safer, stronger
and healthier”. Specifically, a key goal falling under this
priority relates to tackling and preventing anti-social behaviour.
This local lettings plan aligns with this corporate priority, as it
will prevent applicants with a history of anti-social behaviour or
significant unmet support needs from securing these properties
whilst the Local Lettings Plan remains live.
 
Accordingly, in
view of this background context, officers are seeking to introduce
this Local Lettings Plan to support the Council’s wider
placemaking objectives in creating sustainable, cohesive and
resilient communities across the Borough, whilst also recognising
and meeting the Council’s significant rented housing
need.

To ensure that this Local Lettings Plan remains in place for no
longer than required, officers have agreed with Cottsway that this
Local Lettings Plan will automatically expire once all first lets
of the 98 no. affected social rented and affordable rented homes
have been completed, with Cottsway agreeing to write to the Council
to confirm the final lettings completion date within 2 weeks of the
final first let being completed.
topline: The Director of Governance, Housing and Communities has decided to implement a Local Lettings Plan to manage the allocation of affordable homes in a new development in Cheltenham.

content:
The Monitoring Officer began by saying that she was
introducing the report in the absence of the Chair of the
Independent Remuneration Panel (IRP), Graham Russell, who has
decided to stand down from the role. 
She put on record her thanks to him for all his hard work, time and
effort over recent years, which she said was much
appreciated.

Introducing the report, she said that when the new
Cabinet Housing Committee was set up a year ago, it was agreed that
the allowance for the Chair and Vice-Chair would be reviewed after
one year.  As set out in the report, the
panel felt that the special responsibility allowance (SRA) for
these roles should be increased to be in line with that of
regulatory committees (Planning and Licensing) and recommended that
change be made.  

Members were also being asked to note the allowances
paid to co-optees and independent persons on Audit, Compliance and
Governance Committee, Overview and Scrutiny Committee, and Cabinet
Housing Committee.

There were no questions from Members.

A Member said she thoroughly supported the
recommendations, knowing that the amount of technical information
and paperwork dealt with by the Cabinet Housing Committee is very
similar to that of Planning and Licensing.  She was also pleased to note that the independent
persons are being fairly remunerated.

The Leader added her thanks to the outgoing Chair of
the IRP and was sorry to see him go after doing this difficult job
for some years.  She said his vast
experience and knowledge of how councils and councillors work had
made an important and consistent contribution to the work of the
panel, and he will be much missed.

The Mayor also added his thanks on behalf of the
whole Council, saying the task of Chair was challenging and often
thankless.

RESOLVED THAT: 
1.    
the Chair of Cabinet Housing Committee be awarded
a Special Responsibility Allowance of £5,363, to be backdated
to the 1 October 2025;

 
2.    
the Vice Chair of Cabinet Housing Committee be
awarded a Special Responsibility Allowance of £1,823, to be
backdated to the 1 October 2025;

the allowances for co-optees/independent persons
